tools.description: Save creative beats and cast as a production plan for the explicitly approved Script and existing Story. Replaces the full plan; preserve unrelated content. No media or charge. A beat's optional camera plans its shot size, angle and one motivated move (e.g. push-in, tracking, low angle, over-the-shoulder, whip-pan); change size, angle or vantage between neighbouring beats, and do not hold the camera still just because a character speaks. Make a big jump in size or vantage a cut between two beats rather than one large move, which the video model often under-plays. Without it the Shot keeps a static camera. Beats last 3-15 s in 0.5 s steps; video is generated as a source of at least 5 s, trimmed to the beat and quoted as at least 5 s. A character Element's optional voice (e.g. warm, gravelly baritone) shapes how it sounds in every video line. A never-on-screen narrator is a voice Element: it takes a voice too, and its lines use delivery voice_over. Each line has one voice: a voice_over line's voicedBy is video (default; the Shot video speaks it) or narration (a Vixel narration clip speaks it, and the Shot's video leaves it out and keeps only ambience and scene sound). On-screen and sung lines stay in video for lip sync. Choose narration before making the Shot's video; switching later outdates a video made the other way.
tools.name: film_v1_production_plan

tools.description: Quote an image or video for an exact Element or Shot of the Work. This is how agents make media: Vixel prepares prompts and references from the approved Script and production plan. For a Shot video, write the whole take yourself in videoPrompt (up to 7,000 characters), also for retakes after the plan is locked: Vixel sends exactly your text to the video model (line breaks become single spaces, as in every Vixel video prompt) and adds no sentences of its own, while the opening frame, approved Script and price checks still apply; leave out direction, videoDirection and repair, and put the camera, action, approved line word for word and sound in the prompt. What works best on the video model, from its own prompt guide (a guide, not a rule): first the line `For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.`, a blank line, then `integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] …` opening with the art style and the opening frame's subjects and composition, then the action in time order (a later cut as `[Shot 2] At 00:03.500, the camera cuts to …`; camera as motion type plus amplitude and speed, such as `pushes in with large amplitude at medium speed` or `tracks left beside her at walking speed`; each speaker named once with an ID like (S1) and their approved line word for word as <d>[Chinese] …</d>), then `overall_soundscape: …` (ambience, action and wordless sounds) and `non_diegetic_music: …` (N/A when none). Keep the timeline within the Shot's duration and prefer concrete sights and sounds over words like cinematic. Only a video quote without videoPrompt falls back to a take Vixel compiles from direction and the plan, with its own fixed sentences (the exact scripted words, the first frame's identities and no on-screen text); there videoDirection sets that take's camera, action and/or sound (ambience, effects and wordless vocal sounds), an omitted camera or action keeps the Shot's current one and an omitted sound keeps the planned sound. For an image, direction is this take's brief for pose, expression, camera, framing, look and lighting; the identities, the frame shape and no on-screen text stay fixed. An Element image can take referenceAssetIds: images uploaded to this Work, such as the creator's own illustration; say in direction who or what in them this Element is. A Shot opening image can take referenceAssetIds too: extra accepted images of this Work it must match, such as the creator's own model art; say in direction what each one is for. An image take without editAssetId redraws the target from its looks and plan, so it never sees an earlier image. To change one detail of an existing image (wrong scale, a drifted prop, style slips) and keep the rest of it, pass that image as editAssetId (the target's current image or an earlier take of it) and say only the change in direction; a Shot edit may add accepted Element looks as referenceAssetIds to match, such as a character sheet. Media comes in two tiers, Standard by default: an image at options.quality medium or high (HD), a video at options.resolution 768P or 2K (HD, sharper than 1080p, twice the price per second). The quote lists both tiers with their credits in tiers; offer HD when the creator asks for higher quality, 1080p or HD, and quote again with the chosen option before submitting. To remake existing footage (a reference video), cut one 1-15 s window of it (H.264 MP4, at most 32 MB), upload it to the Work (upload_intent with mimeType video/mp4 and durationMs, then upload_finalize) and pass its assetId as options.referenceVideoAssetIds on a Shot video: the take recreates that window's shots, camera, cuts and choreography, with the Shot's accepted looks in place of the original subjects, one for one from the first frame, in the clip's own room. Changing the setting is not supported: a take asked for another place falls back to the original footage. So the Shot's opening image is not sent unless options.useOpeningImage is true, which fits only an image of the cast in the clip's own setting; the quote says which applies. Bind one look per subject in the clip, in the order they appear from left to right, and say in direction who replaces whom. It costs more per second than an ordinary video; the quote shows both tiers. mediaKind audio makes a Shot's narration: its one planned voice_over line, word for word, in the speaker Element's voice bound with element_voice; direction (up to 200 characters) sets pace, emotion and emphasis. Placing a narration line makes narration its voice even if the plan says video: the Shot's videos then leave it out, and one made with the line spoken becomes outdated. No Job, crop, mutation or charge.
tools.name: film_v1_production_quote

tools.description: Read a remake made with remake_generate (its projectId) and move it on as far as the creator approved. Stages: making_look, making_video, finishing (laying the reel's sound), then done; or needs_credits or failed. While Vixel is making something, read it again about every 30 seconds; a remake usually takes 2-4 minutes. When done, result.videoUrl is the finished video: ask the creator to watch it whole. A remake of the creator carries aiLabel: post it only labeled as AI-generated. nextStep says what to offer next (posting, another take). Charges nothing beyond the confirmed order.
tools.name: film_v1_remake

tools.description: Make the remake the creator confirmed: the same inputs as remake_quote plus its quoteId, maxCredits of at least its estimatedCredits, clipRightsConfirmed true (only after the creator said they may use this clip: their own, licensed, or allowed by its creator) and a new stable idempotencyKey. Vixel creates the Work, makes the subject's look from the picture (a remake of the creator uses their photo as it is) and then the take that recreates the window, all within maxCredits; nothing else needs approval. Returns the remake with its projectId and stage; follow it with remake. May spend credits. A retry with the same key returns the same remake and never pays twice.
tools.name: film_v1_remake_generate

tools.description: Start here when the creator wants someone in a trending reel or video: their pet or another animal (subjectKind animal), their own or an original character such as a cartoon, anime, 3D, mascot or toy character (character), or themselves (self). Vixel needs only the reel and one picture of the subject. Do not create a Work, write a Script or plan, cut the video or write prompts; Vixel does all of it on the server. Not allowed: any other real person, celebrities and public figures, anyone under 18, and characters someone else owns (for example Disney, Pokémon or Marvel characters). Give reelUrl (an Instagram or TikTok reel link, or a direct https link to the video file) or clipAssetId (an MP4 the creator uploaded with upload_intent and upload_finalize, for example into the My Assets workspace from ensure_workspace); photoUrl (an image link, or an Instagram post) or photoAssetId (one clear picture of the subject alone); subjectName and subjectKind, with petKind dog, cat or pet for an animal (petName and petKind alone still mean an animal). For two subjects, such as two pets or the creator and their pet, give subjects instead: one entry each with kind, name, photoUrl or photoAssetId, petKind for an animal, isSelf true for the creator, and optionally position left or right (default: the order given, left to right). The reel should show the same number of dancers as subjects (Vixel cannot check it); each subject gets its own look and price, and more than two are refused. For self, ask the creator to confirm the photo is of them and that they are 18 or older, and only then pass subjectIsSelf true (isSelf in subjects); use a personal photo or selfie, not a screenshot, press, stage or magazine picture; the result is labeled as AI-generated. Vixel downloads the video and picks the part it recreates: a video up to 15 s is used whole, a longer one gets the 12 s part with the most movement; pass window (startSeconds, endSeconds; 5-15 s) to choose another part. audio is take (default: the take with the sound the video model made; when posting, use the platform's original sound) or reel (Vixel lays the reel's own sound under the take, matched to its moves). Returns quoteId, estimatedCredits, the window and what will be made. Free: no Work, Job or charge. Next, show the creator the window, the credits and what it makes, ask whether they may use this clip, and call remake_generate.
tools.name: film_v1_remake_quote

tools.description: Make another try of a remake the creator has watched (stage done or failed): a new take from the same look, or a new look and take when there is no look. Show the creator redo.estimatedCredits from remake, and on their yes pass at least that as maxCredits with a new stable idempotencyKey. Returns the remake; follow it with remake. May spend credits; a retry with the same key repeats nothing.
tools.name: film_v1_remake_redo
